name: Young American Creative Patriotic Art Contest
summary: A patriotic art contest for high school students, with national prizes for two-dimensional art and a separate 3-D art category. You don't need a family link to the VFW.
how_to_apply: Make your artwork and turn it in, with the entry form, to a local VFW Auxiliary that takes part in the contest (use the Auxiliary locator). Entries mailed straight to national headquarters are disqualified.
deadline_text: Entries are due to the local VFW Auxiliary by March 31
other_requirements: Must be a lawful permanent resident or have applied for permanent residency with plans to become a citizen (citizens qualify). Must be under 20. Foreign exchange students and past national winners can't enter.

name: Optimist International Oratorical Contest
summary: A speech contest run by local Optimist Clubs in the US, Canada and the Caribbean, with scholarships at the district, regional and World Championship levels. The 2026-27 topic is "How My Actions Strengthen Those Around Me."
how_to_apply: Write and practice a speech on the topic and enter through a local Optimist Club (email programs@optimist.org to find one). Club contests usually finish by late March; winners move up to district, regional and the World Championships in July 2027.
amount_text: District: $2,500 / $1,500 / $1,000 (may vary); regional winners $5,000; World Championship $15,000 / $10,000 / $5,000
deadline_text: Set by each local club; club contests usually end by late March 2027
other_requirements: Must be under 19 on October 1, 2026 and not yet finished high school. International program (US, Canada, Caribbean).

name: Zonta International Young Women in Leadership Award
summary: An international award for young women ages 16 to 19 who lead and volunteer in their communities. Winners move up from local Zonta clubs to district and then 37 international awards.
how_to_apply: Find a nearby Zonta club with the Club Locator and get its deadline and the 2027 application; applications must be typed. If no club is near you, Zonta headquarters or an e-Club can help.
amount_text: 37 international awards of $5,000 each; club and district awards vary
deadline_text: Set by each local Zonta club (check with the club)
other_requirements: Must be 16 to 19 on April 1 and live in a Zonta district. International program; Zonta club members (other than Z club and Golden Z club members) can't apply.

name: SWE Emerging First Year Scholars Scholarship
summary: Scholarships from the Society of Women Engineers for high school seniors starting college in engineering, engineering technology or computer science.
how_to_apply: Apply online through SWE's scholarship portal between February 8 and March 31, 2027. One application considers you for the scholarships you fit.
amount_text: Amounts vary by scholarship (not listed on the main page)
deadline_text: Opens February 8, 2027; due March 31, 2027
other_requirements: Must plan to study engineering, engineering technology or computer science. Some individual awards have their own GPA or school rules.

name: SEG Foundation Scholarships
summary: Merit scholarships for students who plan to study geophysics and earth science toward a career in applied geophysics. High school seniors starting college next year can apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online through SEG's scholarship site; applications open November 1 and close March 1 each year.
amount_text: $500 to $10,000 per academic year (average about $3,200)
deadline_text: Applications open November 1 and close March 1 each year
other_requirements: Needs above-average grades and plans for a college program leading to a career in applied geophysics. Open to students worldwide.

name: WDHOF Basic Dive Training Grants
summary: Grants that pay for learn-to-scuba (open water) certification, a helpful start for future marine biology students. Some grants are set aside for young women 15 to 21 and for people under 21 who can't afford training.
how_to_apply: Fill out WDHOF's online eligibility form and application with two recommendation letters between October 1 and November 30, 2026. You may apply for only one WDHOF scholarship or grant.
amount_text: $1,200 per grant for dive training (some of it can go to basic gear)
deadline_text: Due November 30, 2026, 5:00 pm New York time; awards announced mid-February 2027
other_requirements: Training must lead to a certification from a recognized scuba agency. Funds must be used by August 31, 2028. Open to applicants worldwide.

name: J. Berman Memorial Grant for Sea Turtle Conservation
summary: A grant for a woman of any age to carry out a hands-on sea turtle conservation project. You don't need to be enrolled in a degree program.
how_to_apply: Apply online through WDHOF between October 1 and November 30, 2026 with a clear conservation plan, a specific budget and two recommendation letters.
amount_text: One $2,000 grant
deadline_text: Due November 30, 2026
other_requirements: Money must fund a sea turtle conservation activity (not research), and can't pay tuition or living costs. You may apply for only one WDHOF award.

name: MyImpact Challenge
summary: A national contest for middle and high school students who lead a service, volunteer or small-business project that tackles a problem in their community.
how_to_apply: Lead your project, then submit a pitch video, impact summary, reflection essay and photos through the online portal between September 11, 2026 and April 19, 2027. Groups of up to five can enter together.
amount_text: $10,000 grand prize, $5,000 second, $2,500 third, and up to nine $500 honorable mentions
deadline_text: Closes April 19, 2027, 11:59 pm Pacific
other_requirements: Ages 13 to 19 and enrolled in middle or high school on January 1, 2027. Group entries split the prize.

name: JASNA Essay Contest (High School Division)
sponsor: Jane Austen Society of North America (JASNA)
summary: An essay contest about Jane Austen's novels, open to high school students anywhere in the world. You don't need to be a member.
how_to_apply: The 2027 topic will be posted in November 2026 and submissions open in February 2027; enter on the JASNA website.
amount_text: $1,000 first place (plus a trip to JASNA's annual meeting, travel not included), $500 second, $250 third
deadline_text: 2027 deadline not yet posted; submissions open February 2027
other_requirements: International contest open to students worldwide, including homeschoolers.

name: Federal Junior Duck Stamp Contest
summary: A wildlife art contest for K-12 students: draw a North American duck, goose or swan. State winners go to the national contest, where the top artists win scholarships.
how_to_apply: Make an original 9 x 12 inch hand-drawn piece, attach the entry form (and reference form for grades 7-12), and mail it to the Georgia state coordinator by the state deadline.
amount_text: 2026 national prizes: $1,000 (1st), $500 (2nd), $200 (3rd), $200 (conservation message)
deadline_text: Set by each state coordinator (check the Georgia coordinator's date); usually in spring
other_requirements: Must be a U.S. citizen, resident alien or national. One entry per student. Don't send art to the national office.

name: National Security Language Initiative for Youth (NSLI-Y)
summary: A merit-based U.S. government scholarship to study Arabic, Chinese, Korean or Russian abroad in summer or for a year, or online. Seniors who graduate between December 2026 and June 2027 can still apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online at nsliforyouth.org by November 12, 2026 at 4:00 pm ET. No earlier language study is needed.
amount_text: Scholarship for the study-abroad program (the page doesn't list a dollar value; passport costs not covered)
deadline_text: Due November 12, 2026, 4:00 pm ET
other_requirements: U.S. citizens only (permanent residents can't apply). Must be 15 to 18 at the program start (summer 2027 birthdates July 3, 2008 to June 10, 2012). International study-abroad program.

name: University of St Andrews International Excellence Scholarship
summary: A full-tuition merit scholarship for an international (including US) student starting an undergraduate degree at St Andrews in Scotland in 2027. Biology is one of the eligible schools.
how_to_apply: Apply to a St Andrews course, then use the international undergraduate scholarship form in My Application with a motivation statement and two references by January 27, 2027. You don't need an offer first.
amount_text: Full tuition every year of the degree (one award)
deadline_text: Opened August 17, 2026; closes January 27, 2027
other_requirements: Study abroad in Scotland. Must have overseas fee status. Not for Medicine or the joint William & Mary degree. Winners join the Student Ambassadors Scheme.

name: UBC International Scholars Program
summary: UBC's top awards for international students entering from high school who have all A's and real financial need, including the Karen McKellin International Leader of Tomorrow Award. You're considered for every award you fit.
how_to_apply: Apply to UBC, then submit the International Scholars application by November 15, 2026 (11:59 pm PT). Your school counselor or principal must nominate you and a teacher must give a reference.
amount_text: Award values aren't listed; some awards go up to the full cost of the program and living expenses
deadline_text: Due November 15, 2026; documents by January 31, 2027
other_requirements: Study abroad in Canada. Must be an international student on a Canadian study permit, with all A's, and be nominated by your high school (each school can nominate up to two).

name: University of Glasgow World Changers Global Excellence Scholarship
summary: An automatic merit discount on tuition for international students, including Americans, who get an offer to start a Glasgow undergraduate degree in 2027. The larger award covers Medical, Veterinary and Life Sciences and Science and Engineering.
how_to_apply: No separate application: you're assessed when you get an offer and told within two weeks. Common App applicants can ask the admissions team through the enquiry form.
amount_text: £10,000 a year (Medical, Veterinary & Life Sciences; Science & Engineering) or £7,000 a year (Arts; Social Sciences), renewable
deadline_text: No separate deadline; follows your admission offer
other_requirements: Study abroad in Scotland. Needs international fee status and grades at the program's required level. Can't be combined with most other Glasgow awards.

name: Aberdeen Global Scholarship (Undergraduate)
summary: An automatic tuition discount for new self-funded international undergraduates, including students from the US, starting at Aberdeen in 2026/27 or 2027/28.
how_to_apply: No application needed; the award is applied automatically and shown on your CAS once you're admitted.
amount_text: £6,000 off tuition every year of the degree
deadline_text: No deadline (available until further notice)
other_requirements: Study abroad in Scotland. Must have international fee status and be self-funded, studying on the Aberdeen campus. Not for Medicine, Dentistry or DPLP.

name: Exeter Excellence Undergraduate Scholarship
summary: 150 merit scholarships for international undergraduates starting at the University of Exeter in September 2027.
how_to_apply: Get an offer for an eligible degree, then submit the scholarship web form with a 300-word statement by March 4, 2027 (Round 1). Results come by April 6, 2027.
amount_text: £15,000 off international tuition each year
deadline_text: Round 1 closes March 4, 2027, 11:59 GMT
other_requirements: Study abroad in England. Must have international fee status, be self-funded and hold an offer for an eligible campus-based bachelor's degree (not Medicine). Expected grades around AAB at A level or the equivalent.

name: McGill University Entrance Scholarships
summary: Merit scholarships for first-time undergraduates at McGill in Montreal. Every applicant who meets the grade bar is considered for a one-year award, and you can apply separately for larger renewable awards.
how_to_apply: For the one-year award, just send all your grades with your admission application. For major awards, submit the separate scholarship application in the Applicant Portal soon after applying (opens October 1).
amount_text: One-year award: $3,000 CAD; major renewable awards: $3,000 to $12,000 CAD a year (some limited to Canadians)
deadline_text: Apply soon after your admission application; see McGill's deadlines page
other_requirements: Study abroad in Canada. The $12,000-a-year awards are only for Canadian citizens and permanent residents; the page doesn't say which other major awards US students can get.

name: Joseph S. Rumbaugh Historical Oration Contest
sponsor: National Society Sons of the American Revolution (SAR)
summary: A memorized 5-to-6-minute speech contest about a Revolutionary War event, person or document, for students in grades 9-12. Winners move from local SAR chapters to state and national rounds.
how_to_apply: Find your local SAR chapter (or Georgia's state education chair), get its deadline and forms, and deliver your speech without notes. Chapter deadlines are usually two to four months before the national date.
amount_text: National: $8,000 (1st), $5,000 (2nd), $3,000 (3rd), $500 for other finalists, $200 for other national contestants
deadline_text: Chapter deadlines vary (usually winter); state winners are due to national by May 15
other_requirements: Speech must mention the nation's 250th anniversary and be delivered from memory with no props.

name: DAR Good Citizens Award and Scholarship
summary: Each high school can honor one senior as its DAR Good Citizen for dependability, service, leadership and patriotism. The honoree can then write an essay to compete for scholarships at the chapter, state, division and national levels.
how_to_apply: Teachers and classmates choose the school's honoree; if chosen, you can enter the scholarship round with a personal statement and essay. Ask your counselor or a local DAR chapter for dates.
amount_text: Scholarships at chapter, state, division and national levels (amounts not listed on the current page; DAR reported $5,000 for each national winner in 2022)
deadline_text: Set by the local DAR chapter, usually in fall and winter of senior year
other_requirements: Your school selects you (one senior per school). U.S. citizenship not required.

name: Dr. Aura-Lee A. and James Hobbs Pittenger American History Scholarship
summary: A renewable DAR scholarship for graduating seniors who will concentrate in American history and American government in college. You don't need to be connected to DAR.
how_to_apply: Apply through the DAR online scholarship portal between November 1 and January 31 (11:59 pm Hawaii time), with proof of citizenship, transcript and recommendations.
amount_text: $2,000 a year, renewable for up to four years
deadline_text: Applications accepted November 1 through January 31
other_requirements: Must take at least 24 credit hours in American history and government. Renewal needs a 3.25 GPA. U.S. citizens only; DAR sponsorship not required.

name: Arthur M. and Berdena King Eagle Scout Contest
sponsor: National Society Sons of the American Revolution (SAR)
summary: A national scholarship contest for Eagle Scouts who write a 500-word patriotic essay and complete a family tree chart.
how_to_apply: Download the application, fill out a four-generation ancestor chart, write the essay and send it to your local SAR chapter by its deadline. State winners are due to national headquarters February 15.
deadline_text: Chapter deadlines vary; state winners due to national by February 15
other_requirements: Must be an Eagle Scout registered in an active unit and not turn 19 during the contest year.

name: ASHG DNA Day Essay Contest
summary: An international genetics essay contest (750 words or fewer) for students in grades 9-12. Winning students get cash prizes and their teachers can get lab equipment grants.
how_to_apply: A teacher (or a parent for homeschoolers) submits your essay on ASHG's submission site during the winter window. In 2026 the window ran January 9 to March 4.
deadline_text: 2027 dates not posted yet; in 2026 submissions ran January 9 to March 4
other_requirements: Open to students in the US and other countries; essays in English, one author each.

name: WTS Transportation YOU High School Scholarship
summary: A scholarship for girls in high school who are studying science, technology, engineering and math and are interested in transportation careers.
how_to_apply: Apply through a local WTS chapter (Georgia has a chapter), which sets its own deadline. Chapters submit their winners to the WTS Foundation between December 14, 2026 and January 15, 2027.
deadline_text: Set by your local WTS chapter; chapter nominations are due January 15, 2027
other_requirements: Local chapters may add their own requirements.

name: AISES Indigenous Peoples Education Fund Scholarship
sponsor: American Indian Science and Engineering Society (AISES)
summary: A STEM scholarship from AISES for first-year college students who are enrolled members of a state or federally recognized tribe.
how_to_apply: Join AISES (free for students) and apply in the AISES portal between December 15 and April 30; recommendation letters are due May 7.
deadline_text: Applications open December 15 and close April 30
other_requirements: Must be a full-time first-year student in a STEM field at an accredited college and a current AISES member.

name: AFA Scholarships
summary: Scholarships for graduating seniors and college students in agriculture or food-related degrees who plan careers in food, agriculture or natural resources. Every award includes a spot at the AFA Leaders Conference.
how_to_apply: Apply online through AFA's portal by March 4, 2027; fill in work, activities and service sections fully. Winners are named in early June.
amount_text: $1,600 to $3,200, plus AFA Leaders Conference admission (travel not included)
deadline_text: Due March 4, 2027
other_requirements: Must be 17 to 25 at the time of the conference and plan a four-year degree. A 2.5 GPA or higher is recommended.

name: Women's Western Golf Foundation Scholarship
summary: A four-year scholarship for female high school seniors who play golf, have strong grades and need money for a four-year college. Golf skill isn't judged.
how_to_apply: Apply online from November 1, 2026 with an essay, tax returns, FAFSA, a finance statement, a counselor form with transcript and a recommendation, all by March 1, 2027.
amount_text: $20,000 total ($5,000 a year for four years)
deadline_text: Opens November 1, 2026; due March 1, 2027
other_requirements: Must actively take part in golf and attend a four-year college in the U.S.

name: Sertoma Hard of Hearing or Deaf Scholarship
summary: A scholarship from the service club Sertoma for high school seniors and college students with hearing loss who are working toward a bachelor's degree in any subject.
how_to_apply: Apply online between November 1 and March 31 with an audiogram showing your hearing loss.
amount_text: Amount not listed
deadline_text: Applications accepted November 1 through March 31
other_requirements: Needs at least a 40 dB hearing loss in both ears (shown on an audiogram). U.S. citizens only. Must attend a U.S. four-year college full time.

name: ASHRAE High School Senior Scholarship
summary: Four one-year scholarships for high school seniors starting an engineering or engineering technology bachelor's program that prepares them for heating, cooling and refrigeration (HVAC&R) careers.
how_to_apply: Apply online by May 1 with an official transcript, your college acceptance letter and three signed recommendation letters.
amount_text: $3,000 (four awards)
deadline_text: Due May 1 each year
other_requirements: Need a 3.0 GPA or top 30% class rank. Your college must have an ASHRAE student branch or an accredited (e.g., ABET) program.

name: ASME INSPIRE/Charles W.E. Clarke Scholarship
summary: Scholarships for graduating seniors with financial need who are active in STEM and will study mechanical engineering, mechanical engineering technology or a STEM field.
how_to_apply: Apply online with a transcript that includes first-semester senior grades. Last cycle closed March 15; check ASME's page for 2027 dates.
deadline_text: Last cycle's deadline was March 15; 2027 dates not yet posted
other_requirements: Must enroll full time the fall after graduation in an ABET-accredited (or similar) mechanical engineering or engineering technology program, or other STEM studies.

name: AOPA Foundation High School Flight Training Scholarship
summary: At least 90 scholarships a year for high school students ages 16-18 to earn a private pilot certificate.
how_to_apply: Pass the FAA private pilot written exam, get a free AOPA student membership, then apply online during the fall (October 1 to December 31) or spring (April 1 to June 30) window.
amount_text: $12,000 for flight training on a prepaid card (one section of the page says $10,000)
deadline_text: Fall window October 1 to December 31; spring window April 1 to June 30
other_requirements: Ages 16-18, must have passed the FAA Private Pilot knowledge test and be an AOPA member (free for high schoolers). Funds expire 12 months after the award.

name: FRA Americanism Essay Contest
summary: A 350-word patriotic essay contest for students in grades 7-12. Local winners move to regional and national judging.
how_to_apply: Pick the FRA branch nearest you from the list on the contest page and send your essay and cover sheet to that branch by December 1, 2026.
amount_text: National: $1,500 grand prize; other national winners $1,000, $750, $500
deadline_text: Due December 1, 2026 (2026-27 contest)
other_requirements: Must enter through an FRA member or local branch; homeschoolers welcome.

name: Jean Ibendahl Scholarship (Daughters of American Agriculture)
summary: A scholarship for women ages 18-23 from farm, ranch or agribusiness families (or who work in agriculture themselves) taking courses directly related to agriculture.
how_to_apply: Mail the application starting January 1; it must be postmarked by March 1.
deadline_text: Applications accepted from January 1; postmarked by March 1
other_requirements: Must be 18 to 23 and a farm, ranch or agribusiness woman or her daughter. AAW membership not required.

name: AKC Humane Fund John D. Spurling OBE Scholarship
summary: Tuition help for full-time students in programs that teach responsible pet ownership and dog well-being, such as veterinary medicine, vet tech, animal care, animal behavior, grooming or training.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application (it accepts high school transcripts and a school you plan to attend) and send it by the summer postmark deadline (July 1 in 2026).
amount_text: Five scholarships a year totaling $10,000, paid to the school
deadline_text: Postmark deadline was July 1, 2026; expect a similar summer date in 2027
other_requirements: Must be a full-time student at an accredited U.S. school in a degree or certificate program whose curriculum includes responsible pet ownership.

name: NESA Eagle Scout Scholarships
summary: Merit and need scholarships for Eagle Scouts from senior year of high school on, including the four-year Lawrence S. and Mabel Cooke Scholarship.
how_to_apply: Apply in the NESA portal between December 1, 2026 and February 1, 2027 (11:59 pm CST). Your Eagle board of review must be on or before January 24, 2027.
amount_text: Cooke Scholarship up to $50,000 over four years; other awards $4,000 to $30,000
deadline_text: Due February 1, 2027; winners announced June 10, 2027
other_requirements: Must be an Eagle Scout and active NESA member, enrolled full time in an accredited degree or skilled trade program. Not for military academy students.

name: PHBA Youth Scholarship
sponsor: Palomino Horse Breeders of America (PHBA) Youth Scholarship and Educational Fund
summary: A scholarship for high school seniors who have been Palomino Horse Breeders youth members and plan to go to college or a technical school full time.
how_to_apply: Send the PHBA scholarship form with your transcript, test scores or class rank, two signed recommendation letters, a photo and a personal letter. Check PHBA's site for the 2027 deadline.
amount_text: Amount not listed (plus a $250 award when you finish a bachelor's degree)
deadline_text: Was February 16 in 2025; 2027 date not posted
other_requirements: Must have been a PHBA youth member in good standing for the past two years; one letter must come from a PHBA national director or youth advisor.

name: Robertson Scholars Leadership Program
summary: A full-ride leadership scholarship at Duke and UNC-Chapel Hill, open to students from any state. It covers eight semesters plus funded summers and study abroad.
how_to_apply: Submit the Robertson high school application by November 15, 2026 and apply separately to Duke and/or UNC-Chapel Hill by their deadlines.
amount_text: Full tuition, room and board, and most mandatory fees for eight semesters, plus up to three funded summers
deadline_text: Regular deadline November 15, 2026 (early deadline was October 15)
other_requirements: Must apply to Duke and/or UNC in the same year by their Early or Regular deadlines. Report SAT/ACT scores if you took them.

name: Jefferson Scholarship
summary: A full four-year scholarship to the University of Virginia for seniors with outstanding leadership, scholarship and citizenship. Students can't apply directly; schools in eligible regions nominate one senior.
how_to_apply: Tell your school counselor you're interested; the counselor nominates through the Foundation's portal and materials are due December 1. Check whether your school's region can nominate.
amount_text: Full financial support for four years at UVA, plus enrichment such as study abroad
deadline_text: School nominations and nominee materials due December 1
other_requirements: Nominated by your high school (one per school), and only if your school is in an eligible nominating region. Financial need and citizenship aren't considered.

name: Point Foundation Flagship Scholarship
summary: A scholarship with mentoring for LGBTQ+ students and allies, open to high school seniors heading to an accredited nonprofit U.S. college.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the fall window, which closes November 19 at 5:00 pm PT for funding that starts in fall 2027.
amount_text: Up to $15,000, for up to four years
deadline_text: Window opened September 9; closes November 19, 5:00 pm PT
other_requirements: Must be LGBTQ+ or an ally and enroll full time at an accredited nonprofit U.S. college (not a fully online program).

name: TMCF Enterprise Access HBCU Scholarship
sponsor: Thurgood Marshall College Fund (TMCF) and Enterprise
summary: Need-based scholarships for full-time students in any major, including incoming freshmen, at a TMCF member HBCU in 2027-28.
how_to_apply: Make a two-minute video on how you'll use your education to change the world and apply through the TMCF portal by January 8, 2027. File the FAFSA.
amount_text: Up to $15,000 (81 scholars), paid in fall 2027 and spring 2028
deadline_text: Due January 8, 2027, 11:59 pm EST
other_requirements: Must enroll full time at a TMCF member HBCU (Georgia has several) and have a 2027-28 FAFSA on file.

name: TMCF McDonald's Black and Positively Golden Scholarship
sponsor: Thurgood Marshall College Fund (TMCF) and McDonald's
summary: Need-based scholarships for full-time HBCU undergraduates, including freshmen starting in 2027-28, who show leadership.
how_to_apply: Apply through the TMCF scholarship portal with a 200-word essay by April 23, 2027.
amount_text: Up to $15,000 (60 scholars), paid in fall 2027 and spring 2028
deadline_text: Due April 23, 2027, 11:59 pm EST
other_requirements: Must enroll full time at an HBCU in 2027-28.
